faq.q: Why use titanium for titanium chainring bolt?
faq.a: Grade 5 (Ti-6Al-4V) provides ideal wear resistance, fatigue strength, and 40% weight saving vs steel for drivetrain components. Grade 9 for fasteners requiring cold heading.

faq.q: How is a titanium chainring bolt manufactured?
faq.a: A typical titanium chainring bolt is manufactured using CNC machining of tooth profile; Thread rolling; Swiss-type turning. Each step is critical to achieving the required mechanical properties and dimensional tolerances.

faq.q: What are the alternatives to Grade 5 Ti-6Al-4V for titanium chainring bolt?
faq.a: Stainless steel (heavier, less fatigue life), aluminum (lower strength)

faq.q: What standards apply to titanium chainring bolt?
faq.a: Titanium Chainring Bolt components are typically manufactured to ASTM B348. Additional customer-specific specifications may apply depending on the application and regulatory requirements.

faq.q: What are common failure modes for titanium chainring bolt?
faq.a: Common failure modes include Chainring tooth profile must match chain roller diameter to +-0.05mm for silent shifting; BB spindle taper requires +-0.01mm concentricity for bearing preload accuracy. Proper material selection, manufacturing process control, and inspection mitigate these risks.

faq.q: What surface treatments are available for titanium chainring bolt?
faq.a: Common surface treatments include Passivation ASTM F86. These enhance corrosion resistance, wear properties, and aesthetic appearance.
